questions.q: How does TWAP execution decide how much to trade in each time slice?
options: It sizes each slice proportional to the volume trading at that moment
It splits the order into equal-sized pieces submitted at evenly spaced time intervals, regardless of how much volume is trading
It trades the entire order at the very first opportunity
It only trades when the price matches a specified limit
questions.explain: TWAP (time-weighted average price) execution ignores volume entirely and simply divides the order into equal pieces spread evenly across the execution window by time.

questions.q: What is the key weakness of TWAP execution compared to VWAP execution?
options: TWAP is always slower to complete than VWAP
TWAP trades the same size during thin, illiquid periods as during heavy-volume periods, making its slices proportionally larger relative to available liquidity exactly when liquidity is scarcest
TWAP can never be implemented in practice
TWAP requires knowing the exact closing price in advance
questions.explain: Because TWAP ignores volume and trades equal size at every time interval, its slices become a larger fraction of available liquidity during naturally thin periods (like midday), unlike VWAP, which scales slice size down for illiquid periods.

questions.q: Why does the lesson caution that the VWAP-algo example matching the day's VWAP benchmark almost exactly is "a tell, not a triumph"?
options: Because VWAP algorithms should never match their benchmark

Because the simulation sized slices using realized (already-known) volume, which a real VWAP algo cannot know in advance — it must use a predicted volume profile, and the gap between predicted and realized volume is where real-world tracking error comes from
Because the day VWAP benchmark was calculated incorrectly
Because matching the benchmark means the order was executed at a loss
questions.explain: A real VWAP algorithm sizes slices against a predicted volume profile estimated in advance, not the volume that actually ends up trading. The illustrative code used realized volume, which trivially matches the benchmark — a real algo's shortfall comes from how wrong that prediction turns out to be.

options: The total number of shares that failed to execute
The gap, in basis points, between the price actually achieved and a reference price such as the arrival price
The difference between TWAP and VWAP execution algorithms only
The commission charged by the broker for the trade
questions.explain: Implementation shortfall is the standard way to score any execution approach: the basis-point difference between the execution price actually achieved and a reference price, most commonly the arrival price at the moment the trading decision was made.

questions.q: How does percentage-of-volume (POV) execution differ from both TWAP and VWAP?
options: POV always completes faster than TWAP or VWAP
POV continuously targets a fixed fraction of real-time trading volume, adapting speed to actual market activity, at the cost of uncertain completion time
POV is identical to TWAP but renamed
POV only works for options, never for equities
questions.explain: Unlike TWAP (fixed clock) or VWAP (pre-set volume curve), POV reacts to real-time volume, speeding up in active markets and slowing down in quiet ones — which means, unlike the other two, its completion time isn't guaranteed within a fixed window.
